Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase. The New Zealand players are in a huddle near the ropes before they disperse. They are joined by the two United Arab Emirates openers, Muhammad Waseem and Aryansh Sharma. Tim Southee has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings for New Zealand. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the United Arab Emirates will feel that they are slightly ahead in the game at the halfway stage. The pitch does not have many demons but Muhammad Waseem and Co. will have to bat smartly. On the other hand, New Zealand were unable to finish on a high but they have something to bowl at. Can the Kiwi bowlers rise to the occasion? We shall find out in a bit.

Aayan Khan is in for a chat. He says that the plan was that he should pick wickets and that is what he did and is delighted with his performance as well. Mentions it was moving a bit at the start but states that it has gotten a bit hot now and hopefully it will be easier conditions to bat. Hopes that his side can chase it in 18 overs.

After being inserted into bat, New Zealand were off to a sedate start and the early departure of Tim Seifert made matters worse for them. Moreover, Chad Bowes and the Kiwi middle order surrendered themselves against spin and they found themselves reeling at 65-5. Mark Chapman and James Neesham then got together and forged a solid recovery for the visitors. The duo took their time initially and pressed on the accelerator later to provide impetus to the innings, with Chapman going on to reach his fifty. After Neesham's departure, the boundaries became hard to come by for New Zealand and they could not finish in a fashion they would have liked.

A stunning comeback with the ball from the United Arab Emirates and they have done well to keep the visitors in check. New Zealand end up with their lowest T20I score against a non-Test-playing nation. Coming in for his first game of the series, Muhammad Jawadullah set the tone for the hosts by accounting for the dangerous Tim Seifert in his second over. Muhammad Waseem's move to introduce Aayan Khan inside the Powerplay worked wonders as the young left-arm spinner spun a web around the Kiwi batters. What followed was a quiet period for the United Arab Emirates as Mark Chapman and James Neesham showed immense resistance. The hosts pulled things back well with dismissals of James Neesham and Rachin Ravindra in quick succession which helped them finish strongly with the ball.
Zahoor Khan ends his spell with the slowest of the slower deliveries. It is worked to mid off. The batters take two runs. New Zealand end at 142/8.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set. United Arab Emirates players take the field. Chad Bowes and Tim Seifert come out to open for the Kiwis. Muhammad Jawadullah to start with the new ball.

New Zealand's captain Tim Southee says that they do not have much of a problem in batting first. Mentions that it is more about getting used to the conditions. Informs that they are going with an unchanged side.

Muhammad Waseem, the skipper of the United Arab Emirates informs that they will bowl first. Mentions that the wicket is looking good to bat on. Hopes to restrict the Kiwis on a low total. Informs that he was very happy with the way the boys performed.

New Zealand (Unchanged Playing XI) - Chad Bowes, Tim Seifert, Dane Cleaver (WK), Mark Chapman, Mitchell Santner, James Neesham, Cole McConchie, Rachin Ravindra, Kyle Jamieson, Tim Southee (C), Benjamin Lister.

United Arab Emirates (Playing XI) - Muhammad Waseem (C), Aryansh Sharma (WK), Vriitya Aravind, Asif Khan, Ansh Tandon, Basil Hameed, Ali Naseer, Aayan Khan, Mohammed Faraazuddin, Muhammad Jawadullah (In for Junaid Siddique), Zahoor Khan.
TOSS - The flip of the coin lands in the favour of Muhammad Waseem and the United Arab Emirates have opted to BOWL first.

On the other hand, New Zealand were rocked early, but Tim Seifert's blazing knock got them off to a flying start. Once spinners came on, the visitors' slide began before the 7th wicket stand between Cole McConchie and Rachin Ravindra gave them something to bowl at. With the ball, skipper Tim Southee led the way with a five-wicket haul and saved the Kiwis from an embarrassing defeat. Will New Zealand seal the series with yet another win? Or will the United Arab Emirates hit back? Stick around to find out, as the toss and team news is not far away.

After opting to bowl first, the United Arab Emirates bowled with disciplined lines and lengths and had New Zealand on the ropes before letting them off the hook slightly towards the back end of the innings. In reply, the hosts were off to a decent start, and the chase was going rather nicely with Aryansh Sharma in the middle. However, once Sharma was dismissed, the United Arab Emirates lost their way and fell short by 19 runs. If Muhammad Waseem and Co. are to force a series decider, the batting unit will have to show up collectively.

Hello and a warm welcome, ladies and gentlemen, to our coverage of the 2nd T20I of the three-match series between the United Arab Emirates and New Zealand at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium. In the first T20I, both teams exchanged blows back and forth, but New Zealand ultimately prevailed to take a 1-0 lead in the series.
... MATCH DAY ...

The excitement continues at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium in Dubai as we return for the second T20I of the three-match series that is taking place between the hosts United Arab Emirates and New Zealand. This tie is heavily favoured towards the visiting side as a Test-playing nation but they were given a tough fight by the minnows in the first match comfortably with the visitors winning by just 19 runs thereby taking a 1-0 lead in the series. United Arab Emirates won the toss and elected to field first which seemed like a great decision as they got a wicket on the very first delivery. Tim Seifert scored a half-century and cameos lower down the order from James Neesham, Cole McConchie, and Rachin Ravindra helped them cross the 150-run mark. The hosts would have been thrilled with their bowling effort having restricted a strong batting line-up to an achievable target with Junaid Siddique and Basil Hameed claiming two wickets each. Zahoor Khan and Mohammed Faraazuddin were economical and chipped in with a wicket each. New Zealand returned the favour as Tim Southee dismissed the UAE skipper Muhammad Waseem on a golden duck on the first ball as well and his five-wicket haul helped set up a comfortable win in the end. Vriitya Aravind, Asif Khan, Ansh Tandon, and Ali Naseer all got off to good starts but could not build a long enough partnership with Aryansh Sharma who reached his fifty and held up one end well. In the end, they were bowled out with 2 balls to spare and they will want to put in a better batting performance in this game if they are to stand a chance against their superior opponents. New Zealand will be eager to seal the series in this game itself and not take it to the decider as it would allow them to experiment with their playing 11 in the next match. Will they continue their winning momentum and clinch the series? Or will the United Arab Emirates pull off a remarkable upset? We will find out soon.
